svg.title: Heart rate rises while pace falls, over a flat marathon
svg.desc: Per five-kilometre segment over a flat marathon at six minutes per kilometre, averaged over four seeds. Heart rate climbs from 147.7 bpm in the first segment to 164.0 in the last, while pace slows from 352 to 372 seconds per kilometre, the two lines pulling apart as the race goes on. The measured decoupling of internal to external load is 1.134, inside the published band of 1.16 plus or minus 0.22 from 82,303 recreational marathon runners. The measured second half is 4.25 per cent slower than the first, at the well-paced end of a published range of 5.7 plus or minus 5.4 per cent for smaller samples, and far below the 15.6 per cent mean for men and 11.7 per cent for women across 91,929 finishers.
